name: temporal-determinism-soak
description: Scheduled determinism soak: the functional smoke suites and the guarded-mode frontend probe, fresh same-seed repetitions under host CPU load with choice tracing and diagnostics on
sizing: Capped for a fork's shared hosted-runner quota: each scheduled job runs one workload and seed, always completes two gomad qualify batches at its 32-repetition bound (N = 64 fresh repetitions, so every run compares two batches of each cohort), and starts a third and fourth batch (at most N = 128) only while the previous batch's measured cost plus one fifth of that cost still fits the 120-minute soak budget; one batch is bounded at 55 minutes so the minimum two fit. With the toolchain build, a job stays inside its 180-minute timeout. A defect that diverges one seed-run in 26, the fn-105 D12 rate, fires at least once in 64 fresh runs with probability 1 - (25/26)^64, about 0.92 per workload and seed, and about 0.99 in 128. The report states the N reached, why it stopped, and each batch's execution_wall_nanos. Known inputs: smoke suite executions take about 2 seconds each on linux/amd64 and at most 7 seconds on darwin/arm64 without load (tools/gomad3integration/README.md), but every repetition also prepares its target, and that cost under two busy host threads has not been measured on either platform; the first retained run per platform supplies it. The host loader is two busy threads, the count the runtime host-load conformance tier uses.

informational_platforms.linux/amd64: fn-105 D12 (MILESTONES.md Open findings, linux replay divergence) is open; this platform's soak becomes strict when deferred fn-128.2 closes it
